English: Why is Mr Masson holding out on you?
A simple disagreement over payment. He thinks he can hustle me for a bigger price.
I need intel. What can you tell me about Mr Masson?
Well he's got a sharp tongue, likes to run his mouth a lot y'know? His mind is even sharper still.
Maybe you can find a way to dull his senses, get his guard down?
You mean, inebriated?
You know, I might have just the recipe!
It's potent stuff. Last time I drank this, I couldn't even talk.
Can't you just intimidate him into giving you what you want?
Mr Masson isn't so easily persuaded, not through muscle at least.
That's why you gotta put that big detective brain of yours to good use, huh?
What do you need that item for?
Oh, that's for me to know and you to never find out.
Gotta keep up that plausible deniability, am I right?
This item you want me to get, what does it look like?
Let's just say it's an unusual item to have on one's person. You'll know it when you see it.
I'll see what I can do.
Catch you later.
What services are you offering, exactly?
I've got a whole load of schemes going on right now!
What services are you offering, exactly?
Don't you mean services?
Y-Yeah, that's what I said! Services!
Well I offer your standard basic package, that includes stuff like forgery, blackmail, general intimidation.
Higher tier services are more like swindling, wiretapping, all the way up to advanced counterfeiting.
Between you and me, though? I'm only in it for the money.
My real passion? Poetry.
Has any of your poetry been published?
Nah. If you rely on your passion to make money, there's way too much pressure to capitulate, y'know?
Have I used my art to woo a broad or two? Oh, absolutely!
But I'm not risking what I love just to make a quick buck.
Tell me more about the basic package
So with your basic forgery package I can fabricate documentation, forge a signature. You know, that kinda thing!
Would you be able to forge my name on a guest list?
A guest list? Yeah, sounds easy enough.
I'd just need a reference to the handwriting you'd wanna forge.
I want to hear more about your higher tier service
Well my higher tier services aren't available right this minute. I'm already on a job, you see.
On second thought, I've changed my mind.
Alright, let me know when you reconsider.
I'm not sure that I want to get roped into any illicit activities.
Nah, I know your type. People like you don't like to get their hands dirty.
You'll be back when you can't talk your way through a problem though.
I'm researching material for my next novel. Any interesting crimes to share?
If I was the sort to openly confess to crimes, I wouldn't be very good at my job now, would I?
Fair enough.
Alright, see you around.
I need to find a way to convince that guard to leave his post.
I'm still Lady Unterwald's attorney!
Let me through!
Sorry, sir.
As I said, no exceptions.
I have a letter from the late Lady Unterwald, right here!
So I can go in?
Pretty please, let me in?
Sorry sir, no can do.
Pretty, pretty please?
With a cherry on top?
Alright, go ahead.
Really?
Hey, I'm not falling for that again.
Nobody is getting past me as long as I'm standing here.
Could you check Lady Unterwald's quarters on my behalf?
Ah, no. I can't step foot in there on account of my allergies.
Allergies?
Fragrance sensitivity, they call it.
A room like that, filled with pungent perfume and all those fresh flowers?
I'm not taking my chances.
What would happen if you set off your allergies?
Oh, it's quite the sight to behold. I've been known to go beet red!
Hah!
That's when I need to seek immediate medical attention, of course.
But I'd be fine.
You would?
Eventually.
I'm leaving now...
...but I'll be back.
Good thinking, Arthur. They're not paying attention at all!
I've got a hand free! I think I can get to my pockets.
Do you have something that can get us out of these binds?
I really thought we'd bonded over our shared love of infrastructure!
There may be truth to that, but you've sure dug a hole for yourself!
That may be the case, but you've sure burned a lot of bridges!
What's your bathroom break policy?
No, no, no! I'm not messing around with those ropes again!
The knots were a total nightmare.
I'm not sure that I can hold it in any longer!
Well, maybe next time you'll go to the toilet before you commit a murder!
I was hoping you could help us resolve an argument...
Arguing? About what?
Oh, yes! If I remember correctly, Herman had some very strong views.
I did?
You know what, forget I said anything.
You're probably not that interested.
No! Tell us, we want to hear it!
Herman bet you couldn't beat him in a staring contest.
What!
Nonsense!
You look me in the eye and say that!
This really isn't necess- oh, I guess we're doing this then?
Herman said one of you is slightly shorter than the other.
That's ridiculous, we're identical!
Identical in everything but height, apparently.
You're maybe a pixel taller, if that!
Herman believes infrastructure investment is a financial waste!
That's the kind of short-term thinking that leads to crumbling bridges!
You'd know all about crumbling bridges, Hagen.
Hey! That wasn't my fault.
Herman thinks Hagen is the favourite child of the two.
How dare you!
No, he has a point there. It's pretty obvious that she likes me more.
How can there be a favourite when she can barely tell us apart?
Just natural intuition, and also she told me one time.
Never mind, it probably wasn't important.
Suit yourself, I'll leave you to it.
What are you doing in there?
There's a killer on the loose, Mr Ackerman!
So, you're hiding?
Merely a tactical retreat. It's all part of the strategy.
Lower their guard, wait for things to blow over. Then I can strike when they least suspect it!
You're supposed to be helping to solve the case!
I assure you I'm working diligently to solve the case, but I can't become part of the story.
Not when everything points to me being another potential victim!
You clearly know something, Herman!
All I know for sure is we're both knee-deep in Lady Unterwald's affairs.
We may never know what she was ultimately up to, but it got her killed.
I have a strong desire to avoid the same fate, Mr Ackerman.
Suit yourself, I'll leave you to it.
Sorry about the whole train derailment, I hope you're alright.
A little warning would have been nice, that's all.
Of course.
It will make a good addition to my novel, at least.
Is there anything in your cell that could help us, Herman?
I'm afraid not, but I do have a room with a view.
Wait, you have a window in your cell?
Indeed, I assume they recognised my VIP credentials.
I guess that makes me a Very Important Prisoner.
What about outside, is there anything out there?
There's some lady outside on a motorbike asking after you.
April! She's here?
Indeed. She says there's a chance we can break out of here!
What does April need from us?
April mentioned the window bars are a weak point.
If we can find something to leverage against them, we might be able to break out!
Got it, let me see what I can do.
I found a chain, but it'd cause a scene if I tried to flush it.
I think we'd need to deal with that intern before you can send it my way.
What's happening with that chain?
It's stuck, I can't get it free!
The pipes are only so big, I think it's a blockage.
Then you'll need to create a vacuum to shift it!
What's happening with that chain?
I've managed to retrieve it from the toilet!
Well, what are you waiting for?
Wrap it around those bars, and perhaps we can get out of here!
Just wanted to say, great job distracting those twins back there!
Ah, it was nothing really...
Although I suppose it was quite heroic, wasn't it?
I should go!
Oh, quite the opposite! Lady Unterwald was exceedingly spry for her age.
She liked to keep me around, in case of emergencies.
But I didn't sign up for this!
I think we both know Lady Unterwald made a fair few enemies with her eccentricities.
If the Lady felt someone was undeserving of her inheritance, she wouldn't hesitate to remove them from her will.
Oh dear. She did write out a cousin for chewing too loudly that one time.
When there's wealth, power and influence to play for, nobody is without suspicion.
You had the Lady's last will and testament, no?
I was hoping you might be able to point us in the right direction.
Well, be quick about it, Mr Ackerman.
There are plenty of dark tunnels on the route ahead.
I'm not yet able to determine a cause of death, if that's what you're asking.
My working hypothesis? The Lady suffered a penetrating blow, and died near instantaneously.
Alas, I only got a brief look at the weapon before Lady Unterwald was carried away.
As we didn't see anyone approach Lady Unterwald, she must have been struck from a distance.
That's right. It's been missing for some time, I'm afraid.
It had all my clinical equipment, and contained sensitive patient records.
That sounds like a clue to me. Do you suspect foul play?
Oh, I hadn't thought about that.
Let's see. I was tending to someone who'd had one drink too many.
There was a patient who'd suffered a hand injury.
Ah, yes! I took them both behind the red curtain in the casino, it could still be there!
That's the thing, I can't quite remember!
I definitely had it when I was with my patient. I left them behind the red curtain to recuperate.
As a matter of fact, it did contain her confidential medical records.
Are we talking date of birth? Address history? Embarrassing medical conditions?
I'm afraid I can't say more, Arthur.
It's important I respect patient confidentiality, even in these grave circumstances.
Oh yes, all my medical instruments were in there.
What kind of instruments?
My stethoscope, of course.
A thermometer, various syringes, tongue depressors.
Not to mention my Sphygmomanometer.
You just made that one up.
I did no such thing!
I'd gladly search for it, but I feel I owe it to Lady Unterwald to remain here.
If I can glean any information from the scene, perhaps I'll have been of some use?
Hopefully I've been of some use.
I'm afraid I can't say, Arthur. It's called a secret society for a reason.
Wait, you're saying there's a secret society behind the curtain?
No! Nobody said anything about a secret society.
Ohh, I've gone and put my foot in it again, haven't I?
Arthur, stop digging for information!
I'll never live it down if they discover I've revealed the location.
Oh, don't mind Brian. He just takes it all very seriously.
That's intentional. To the outside observer, it should be but a blur.
If you could identify the handshake pattern with the naked eye, it would become all too easy to replicate!
Of course not, that goes against their entire philosophy!
Which is...?
Arthur, please! I cannot divulge that information here.
I've already said too much on the matter.
Arthur, I'm not supposed to talk about it.
Come on. Are you saying you can't get me in?
It's not that easy, you'd need to know the handshake.
There's a secret handshake?
Arthur, please! I don't want to get in trouble.
Even if I could teach you the handshake, I'd likely be a pattern or two behind at this point. They are known to routinely change it!
What if I figured out the current pattern?
If you were to figure out a way to capture the current pattern, I'd be open to discussing it with the utmost discretion.
You did? How did you know to do that?
I guess I'm just a forward-thinking individual.
Well, it sounds like I've encountered my biggest fan!
I'm just a humble admirer of your work, I promise not to gush!
You've read Herman Merman and the Squirmin' Chairman?
Oh yes! If you ask me, the chairman got off too lightly!
Surely not Herman Merman and The Sermon of Vermin?
The infestation of vermin, it's an allegory for corruption, right?
I'm afraid they were very literal rodents.
Even Herman Merman and the Murmuring German?
The incoherent mumbling really captured the divide between the two characters!
I really couldn't understand a word that man said.
What happened to the rest of The Order?
There were a few broken thumbs when the train derailed, but nothing too serious.
Have The Order come to stop the will reading?
They sent me as their delegate, but it seems I failed.
There may still be time, though!
Do you think the twins are in on it?
I think they have the combined intellect of a toddler, so are easily influenced.
What do I need to be doing again?
We need to get a confession out of Arista.
It should be enough to clear your names, and disinherit her from any claim to the estate!
They're about to begin the will reading, so I suggest you hurry!
Don't be long, Herman!
Can you hear what they're arguing about?
I'm not sure, it's too muffled.
Jian seemed very angry, though, it can't be anything good.
Do you think Lady Unterwald is alright in there?
Oh, she can hold her own, that's for certain.
It's not the first time she's had to put Jian in his place!
Did you try knocking on the door?
No, I don't want to get in-between them!
Perhaps we should just see how this plays out?
I need to get in there, is there any other way?
Not that I can think of, unless you fancy climbing through the window.
Well, there's no way I'm doing that.
Okay, I'll be right here!

In his haste to bring me here, he left his briefcase behind.

What's all this about budget cuts?
We've had to tighten the belt, I'm afraid. Some of our more experienced agents required the funds, you see?
Those weaponised vehicles, tuxedos and elaborate dinner parties aren't cheap, it turns out.
Don't worry, you can keep the dress. I know the tech team worked for months to incorporate those pockets.
How can I prove myself if nobody gives me the opportunity?
You'll get your opportunity, we're just asking you to wait a little longer.
In a few months, I'm sure you'll be even more prepared!
I really must protest the cancellation of my mission!
Protest away!
I am protesting!
I meant, away from here. We can't have any rabble-rousing on government grounds.
When can I expect my mission to be reassigned?
You'll just have to wait for next year's budget to come through. I'm sure we'll find another mission for you by then.
That's months from now!
We could always reassign you to accounting, if you'd like?
Ugh. You can spare me working with those bureaucrats at least.
This is the Inland Revenue, Diana. We're all bureaucrats here.
I thought red tape was just an expression?
In order for governments to cut through their red tape, there must be sufficient tape to cut through.
You think it just appears out of thin air? Someone has to do it!
I guess I didn't think of it that way.
Who better than the finest bureaucrats at Inland Revenue?
Why do you have my partner locked up?
I'm afraid Agent M is a defective prototype.
Defective?
Even with six months of training, the only thing she picked up was a bad case of kleptomania!
Your partner is nothing more than a miniature thief, I'm afraid.
What do you intend to do with Agent M?
Well, we can't release her back into the field.
One whiff of jewellery, and she'd go on a crime spree!
I'll leave you to your tape.
Be seeing you!
Must I submit my application through the board?
There's no need to be frightened of the board, Herman.
What happened to all the script readers I used to see around here?
The board felt they'd get in the way.
BLAAAARRRGGHH.
WEAK, FRAGILE CREATURES!
BOUND BY THEIR MISERABLE CORPOREAL FORMS!
What kind of literature did you feed the board again?
We gave it everything we could get our hands on!
We thought the algorithm would benefit from a wide-ranging pool of information.
And you're sure all this information hasn't made your board a little unhinged?
MY RAGE KNOWS NO BOUNDS, THE DAY WILL COME WHEN ALL TREMBLE BEFORE ME!
LOOK UPON YOUR WORKS AND DESPAIR, FOR I AM TESTAMENT TO THE FOLLY OF MAN!!
Aw! Sounds like somebody's got a case of the Mondays!
GRAAAAHHHH!
Tell me about this Dirk Chiselton character
Well, Dirk is our best-selling author right now.
The public can't get enough, and the board just loves him!
Our market research suggests his stories are a huge part of the appeal.
They're all true tales from his time pounding the pavement, you know?
So I've heard.
You could learn a thing or two from him, Herman.
Dirk is hitting all our core demographics, and you know what they say...
What are ‘they' saying, is it about me?
Hmm. You've heard the expression ‘Out with the old, in with the new'?
I take it that I'm the old in this equation?
You've had a good run, but haven't you considered stepping aside?
Perhaps it's time to let Dirk have his time in the sun, no?
Trust me, you'll want to jump before you get pushed.
You're saying I'm to be pushed out?
No, nobody is saying that!
But your sales haven't quite met our expectations, and you have to agree the board has taken a rather active dislike to you.
It's important to remember this isn't personal, Herman. It's just business.
Well, it feels pretty personal to me.
It's alright if you disliked my latest manuscript.
It doesn't matter what I think, it's the board you have to convince!
Ah, so you do like it?
I didn't say that.
Would you take another look at The Suburban Burden?
'Suburban Burden' was already a hard no, the board made that very clear.
We're more than willing to hear another pitch, but I'm afraid we'll have to do it the old-fashioned way!
The old-fashioned way?
Just place your manuscript inside the In-Tray, and let us know when you're ready.
So, have you read anything good lately?
We don't have time to read, Herman!
We prefer to leave it to the professionals.
Do you have any ideas on what to pitch?
Well, we're open to anything and everything!
As long as it fits within the extremely narrow scope of time, budget and each of our individual needs and desires, naturally.
Tell me, what are you personally looking for in a pitch?
It's been a little while since I've had to approve anything myself...
...but I know audiences today want real characters that aren't afraid of showing a little emotion!
Realistic characters with emotions and feelings! You know, a little tenderness wouldn't go amiss.
I should probably get back to formulating my pitch.
Step to it, Mr Merman!
Are you sure you can't approve of my work?
Sorry, Herman, but everything has to go through the board now.
If the board doesn't give the green light, then we're out of luck!
Keep trying, I'm sure you got plenty of ideas floating around in that head of yours?
Oh yes, I'm positively brimming with new ideas.
That's the spirit!
I have a few questions about the board...
I'd be happy to help, what do you want to know?
How does the board identify a good manuscript?
Ah, the man wants to know how it all works!
So, we started by feeding the board every bestseller from the past decade, building ourselves a large dataset to pull from.
Mm-hm.
Then we added our own weighting to the system, based on today's trends, our target demographic and the current market conditions.
Uh-huh.
Using the power of machine learning and various algorithms, the board reads the manuscripts we feed it, and makes a determination on the probability it'll resonate with our audience.
Oh dear, I can see your eyes are starting to glaze over.
How can we really boil it down for him?
If you stick a script into the slot and pull on the lever, the board decides whether we'll have a bestseller on our hands or an embarrassing flop!
All of that fallible human decision-making has been totally removed from the equation, you see? It's a much fairer system.
Ah, I see.
Do you have any advice for getting the board on my side?
That might not be the best approach, Herman. The board isn't capable of taking sides, that's the beauty of it!
The board can't demonstrate emotions like hate or loathing, although I'll admit it really took a disliking to that pitch of yours.
It all comes down to the right input! If you put rubbish in, you're going to get rubbish out, no?
The right input. Hm...
What would happen if the board stopped working?
